Title: Move OnFinalize callback outside engine global lock
Description:
THROUGHPUT BOTTLENECK + DEADLOCK RISK. CandleEngine.finalizeCandleLocked calls cfg.OnFinalize(candle) while holding e.mu.Lock(). OnFinalize (handleFinalizedCandle) then:
  a) sends to candleDBFlushCh (non-blocking, OK)
  b) sends to indicatorManagerInputCh (non-blocking, OK)
  c) calls broadcastCandle() which calls candleWsClients.Range() with per-client channel sends

The entire WS broadcast runs under the engine lock. Under high-speed simulation with 9 intervals × N instruments, the engine is stalled for the broadcast duration on every candle finalization.

FIX:
1. In finalizeCandleLocked, copy the OpenCandle value to the stack (or take ownership of the pointer) then release e.mu before calling OnFinalize:
   candleCopy := *candle  // copy while locked
   e.mu.Unlock()
   e.cfg.OnFinalize(&candleCopy)
   e.mu.Lock()  // re-acquire if loop needs it

2. Better approach: queue finalized candles to a dedicated `finalizeQueue chan *OpenCandle` and process callbacks in a separate goroutine. This fully decouples the engine tick loop from I/O.

3. Ensure OpenCandle.mu is not held across the callback boundary.
Notes: Resolves the main throughput bottleneck at high simulation speed.

Title: Fix StartSystemMonitor goroutine leak — add context cancellation
Description:

Title: Fix candle volume: use tick.Volume delta instead of LastTradedQuantity
Description:
WRONG VOLUME IN ALL 9 TIMEFRAMES. candle_engine.go lines 153 and 169:
  Volume: float64(tick.LastTradedQuantity)  // open
  candle.Volume += float64(tick.LastTradedQuantity)  // update

LastTradedQuantity is the size of the last individual trade (e.g. 50 shares). Accumulating it inflates volume on duplicate ticks and is not the canonical candle volume metric.

The correct approach uses tick.Volume (cumulative day volume from exchange):
  candleVolume[token] = tick.Volume - prevVolume[token]

1. Add to CandleEngine struct:
   lastVolume map[uint32]uint32  // token -> last known cumulative volume

2. In ProcessTick, compute delta before updating candles:
   delta := uint32(0)
   if prev, ok := e.lastVolume[token]; ok && tick.Volume >= prev {
       delta = tick.Volume - prev
   } else {
       delta = tick.LastTradedQuantity  // fallback for first tick or OI reset
   }
   e.lastVolume[token] = tick.Volume

3. Replace all Volume references in the new-candle and update-candle paths with float64(delta).

4. On market open (day rollover), reset lastVolume[token] = 0.

5. Write unit test: feed 3 ticks with Volume=1000, 1500, 2200 → 1m candle volume should be 1200 (2200-1000).

Title: Fix tickSequenceCounters unbounded memory growth — replace time.Time key with epoch-second
Description:
MEMORY LEAK. ingest.go tickSequenceCounters:
  map[uint]map[time.Time]int

At 8x simulation with 10 instruments: each unique time.Time becomes a map key. At 80 ticks/sec, 288,000 keys/hour accumulate before cleanup. Each time.Time = 24 bytes → ~7MB/hr, potentially 50MB+ in long sessions.

The cleanup interval is 1s with expiry 2s — but cleanup holds sequenceMux while iterating the entire map, blocking processTick.

FIX:
1. Change inner map key from time.Time to int64 (Unix second):
   tickSequenceCounters map[uint]map[int64]int
   key := tick.EventTime.Unix()  // granularity = 1 second

2. This reduces unique keys to at most 1 per instrument per second, bounded to ~10 entries per instrument at any given time.

3. Ensure cleanup uses the int64 key:
   if now.Unix()-ts > int64(expiryDuration.Seconds()) { delete(...) }

4. If sub-second sequence tracking is needed, use a ring buffer of fixed size (e.g., last 1000 ticks per instrument) instead.
Notes: Fixes memory leak. Cleanup lock contention also reduced.

Title: Replace sync.Map for wsClients with RWMutex + typed map for better Range performance
Description:
PERFORMANCE. sync.Map is optimized for keys that are written once and read many times, or for cases where keys are disjoint across goroutines. For wsClients (high write rate during connect/disconnect, high read rate during Range), a standard map with RWMutex is faster.

FIX:
1. Replace `wsClients *sync.Map` in MarketDataIngestor and CandleGenerator with:
   wsClientsMu sync.RWMutex
   wsClients   map[*websocket.Conn]chan []byte

2. Update Register/Unregister to use mu.Lock() and the typed map.

3. In the broadcast worker, take mu.RLock(), copy the map entries to a local slice, release RLock, then iterate the slice for sends. This avoids holding the lock during channel sends.

4. Update Hub in realtime/hub.go to pass the new typed map or use a consistent wiring pattern.
Notes: Reduces GC pressure from sync.Map internal dirty/read map churn.

Title: Implement IV Rank and IV Percentile for options strategy selection
Description:
IV Rank and IV Percentile are the most important filters for options strategy selection. High IV = sell premium. Low IV = buy premium.

  IV Rank     = (current IV - 52-week low IV) / (52-week high IV - 52-week low IV) * 100
  IV Percentile = % of days in past 252 trading days where IV was below current IV

      CurrentIV    float64

  SELECT MAX(iv) as high_iv, MIN(iv) as low_iv,
         PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY iv) as median_iv
  FROM option_chain_snapshots

Title: Generate synthetic option prices in simulation mode using Black-Scholes
Description:
In simulation mode, real Kite tick data is not available. Options prices need to be generated synthetically from the simulated underlying price.

   optionPrice = BSPrice(S=currentPrice, K=strike, T=daysToExpiry/365, r=0.065, sigma=simulatedIV)

2. simulatedIV = baseIV + randomWalk (mean-reverting, default baseIV=0.15)
